name: City Council Workshop
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council Budget Workshop

  January 16, 2015

A Budget Workshop of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to
order by Mayor Schlicht at 9:02 a.m., on January 16, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 1, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Susan Knudson, Budget and Purchasing Analyst
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Boyd Steele, M.V.: requested that the Council consider funding a special musical event at the
Murray Center. The presentation would be non-denominational and he offered to provide further
information and a music CD at the Council’s request. The estimated cost is $1,500 per performance
on a monthly or quarterly basis and he stated that he is personally willing to fund one event.
City Council Minutes  1  January 16, 2015
 Sharon Cody, M.V.: announced that the Animal Services Center handles adoptions as well as
police-type service. The field officers protect citizens, dogs who are bitten or hit by cars, and tend
to wildlife issues. 23% of the services are paid for by the City's general fund and it is a community
facility with 16 paid staff members, 100 weekly volunteers, 22 vets who have contributed over $2
million in free veterinary services, as well as a dog trainer. She noted that the non-profit group
DAWG does great things and has raised $1.2 million to help the animals at the shelter.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked staff to identify the developers or projects listed in the Housing
Authority Annual Report on the January 19, 2015, City Council Agenda. He stated that there is a
slush fund of $8.9 million in assets, yet there are obligations for park restrooms and the Nadadores
facility rehabilitation. He recommended starting with two or three park restrooms and asked why
the Housing Authority agency is kept going and why it wasn’t listed on the agenda topics for today.

David Selecky, Commissioner for AYSO Region 84, M.V.: announced that AYSO Region 84 is
celebrating its 40th anniversary and he attributed that success, in large part, to the cooperation that
they have with the City. Having been commissioner for 4 years and an AYSO volunteer for almost
20 years, he stated that he is confident that Mission Viejo has the best fields in Orange County.
Mr. Selecky asked that the City continue to maintain and make the fields available as they currently
are.

BUDGET WORKSHOP

1.  Introduction from Staff

  City Manager Wilberg introduced the facilitator for the budget workshop, Sherry Lund.

  Facilitator Lund outlined the ground rules for the day.

2.  Proposed Budget Calendar

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the proposed budget calendar.

  By consensus, the Council asked for preliminary progress along the way.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern that the budget it not scheduled to be approved until
  July 6, 2015, when the current budget expires on June 30.

  Director Dyas noted that it is not uncommon to do this and staff would lose three weeks
  in the process if the adoption date were moved up. A resolution allowing for interim
  spending is put in place whenever the budget is adopted after July 1.

3.  Mission, Vision and Organization Values

City Council Minutes  2  January 16, 2015
   Council Member Sachs stated that the values are very subjective and he asked staff to look
  at them from an objective standpoint when scoring against them.

  By consensus, the Council confirmed that the City’s mission, vision and values should
  remain the same.

4.  Strategic Goals

  The Council Members discussed the strategic goals and agreed that there are potential
  additional goals which need to be considered in a different meeting outside of this
  workshop.

6.  OCSD Contract

  All Council Members indicated that they are satisfied with the current OCSD contract
  level.

  Other Council questions and observations:

    Look into providing emergency vehicle preemption activators for the Sheriff’s
  cars (like those used for fire trucks.) Would this be a County expense or a City
  cost?
    What are the relative costs of motorcycle units vs. cruisers?
    Look at the City of Laguna Hills audit (benefits and efficiencies.)
    Continue to push for electronic citation devices and other technology uses to
  enhance services/improve efficiencies.
    Note that cities report crime differently, so it may be difficult to make meaningful
  comparisons. What are best practices in other safe cities?
    Note that all costs to maintain motors come from the City, not the County.

7.  Landscape Maintenance

  Four of the five Council Members were in favor of increasing the funding level for slope
  maintenance (Council Member Sachs was satisfied with current level.) All agreed that
  Alicia Parkway should be the next slope rehabilitation project. Mayor Schlicht stated that
  she would like to see Muirlands rehabbed after Alicia.

  Other Council questions and observations:

    Are there opportunities for grant funding? Typically not for slopes (per staff.)
    If Alicia Parkway is chosen, would Council wish to start at the east or west end?

City Council Minutes  3  January 16, 2015
     The City should consider safety/tree work too (staff noted that this is actually an
  Urban Forestry issue rather than slope maintenance).
    Walls could be cleaned and painted on Muirlands Blvd. when this project is
  funded.

RECESS

At the hour of 10:24 a.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 10:41
a.m. with all five City Council Members present.

8.  Pavement Management Program/Traffic Management

  Council Member Ury was absent during this item.

  When asked about service/spending levels, Mayor Schlicht requested that more money be
  spent on pavement/traffic management. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said spend less. Council
  Members Bucknum and Sachs said the spending amount is just right.

  Staff noted that the City plans to reinstate the Gas Reserve by the end of the year with
  Council guidance. It would return to its former levels of 30% of revenue.

  Pavement questions and observations:

    Bidding for work – we should not rely on the same vendors over and over.
    Are there performance requirements in contracts to assure the quality of work?
    There are concerns about the 5 yr./7yr. cycle. Mayor Schlicht had “alligatoring”
  on her street, which has been paved only twice in 30 years. What is more cost-
  effective, a 5-year or a 7-year cycle? (Staff will provide more information at a
  later date.)
    Lake Forest uses a deeper overlay of paving. Is that more effective?
    How often is resurfacing done and is it uniform? Mayor Pro Tem Raths observes
  that paving sometimes seems to happen on perfectly good roads.

  Traffic flow questions and observations:

    Look at new flow-based systems vs. time-based systems. Inter-agency efforts to
  understand and look at new technologies.
    Who does traffic synchronization?
    Where have synchronizations been done?
    Who coordinates ramp traffic?
    Just get traffic moving more quickly.

City Council Minutes  4  January 16, 2015
     Traffic management is important for residents around the apartments near the
  Country Club. Council would like to see the numbers on amount of traffic that
  will be added with the addition of the apartments.

10.  Special Events/Community Support

  The City Council members asked questions about funding for the Mission Viejo Activities
  Committee.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked if Bunny Days and Hometown Halloween are included in the
  SVUSD Kids Factory program.

  Council Member Bucknum noted that she is generally happy with the current spending
  for special events. Mayor Schlicht and Mayor Pro Tem Raths said they are in favor of
  lowering funding for special events and Council Member Sachs would like spending to
  be about the same and noted that the City’s events are a benefit to residents. Council
  Member Ury said he is comfortable with current spending and agreed that the events
  benefit residents.

  In reference to the Community Services Grant Program, Mayor Schlicht questioned one
  government organization funding another one like Saddleback College. She also stated
  that 100% of the money should go to direct program costs, not for administration costs.

  Other Council questions and observations:

    Who is the Mission Viejo Activities Committee? Last fiscal year the City gave
  them $249,000, which includes holiday street lights.
    Further discuss wheelchair tennis tournament. It should not be funded by the City
  (Council Member Sachs.)
    Council Member Bucknum suggested having a presentation to hear all relevant
  information on wheelchair tennis before making a decision.
    Mayor Schlicht suggested that the Symphony find sponsors.
    We address some of the 30 different communities that make up Mission Viejo at
  any given event. (Council Member Ury)

9.  Economic Development

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that cities have competition from other cities and the
  economic/redevelopment that is done nearby. He stated that it would take a lot of skill to
  convince the owners of the property across the street that upgrading will have a reward.

  Other Council questions and observations:

City Council Minutes  5  January 16, 2015
     The Council is unified in wanting to increase spending in Economic Development.
  Council Member Bucknum added her desire to focus on prioritizing and liked the
  proposal by Buxton.
    The Council is interested in revitalization of the area across from the Civic Center.
    What can the City do? What needs to be done? We need to be competitive so we
  are the City being talked about and give people a reason to move here.
    The Chamber and Business Expo could provide more outreach.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: commented on the first half of the meeting and discussions regarding
police costs. He suggested that staff should dedicate the most amount of effort to savings in that
area and look at the cities that have done studies without sacrificing safety. He also recommended
looking at cost sharing ideas. Lastly, Mr. Wontrobski stated that the Felipe Tennis Center should
be shut down or the hours of operation should be cut.

RECESS FOR LUNCH

At the hour of 12:13 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting for lunch. The City Council
reconvened at 12:39 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

11.  Recreation Memberships

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: recommended that the City publicize the recreation centers more.

  Council questions and observations:

    How does recreation attract people to the City? It’s linked to Economic
  Development.
    It’s most effective in making it appealing for citizens to live here.
    Are there any subsidies on Recreation? The Council would like a list.
    Look at privatizing facilities.
    There are needs for youth—low cost or no cost places to hang out.
    Out of Bounds (Scott Ramirez) is a good resource.
    Look at cost recovery fees.
    Is there elasticity for increasing fees? Look into this. Also look into the
  opportunity for kids where they can play tennis in off hours for $1 or for free with
  no membership. Clinics could be provided for them. If there is such a high interest
  in tennis in the community, we should look at fully utilizing facilities.
    Look for a way for youth to congregate outside of sports.

City Council Minutes  6  January 16, 2015
 12.  MVTV Programming/Community Relations

  Helen Workun, M.V.: expressed support for the continuation of the Breakfast with Gary
  and Kelly TV show at the Murray Center.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she enjoys MVTV Channel 30 but doesn't think the
  wheelchair tennis event should be televised with the single camera view.

  By consensus, the Council Members agreed with the current level of programming for
  MVTV.

  Other Council questions and observations:

    There is no leverage with Cox and we don’t have strong data on who’s watching.
    Council Member Bucknum would like to see the Jazz music show stay in the City
  (this is done in collaboration with Saddleback Community College).
    When we subsidize KSBR, what are we losing in room rental? Are we losing
  revenue?
    Can corporate advertising support any of this or are there restrictions?
    Work with the Chamber.
    An excellent tool for City’s youth, e.g., camera operation, production at the same
  time contributing to programming.
    Need guidelines on sponsorship and advertising from the City Attorney. Is it
  allowable to recoup expenses through advertising?
    What is the cost to seek sponsorships?

  By consensus, the Council Members expressed support for the current City publications
  (Outlook, Mission Viejo Life and the Annual Report.)

  Other Council questions and observations:

    Council Member Ury stated that he would like to see more push media and give
  residents an option to receive the Annual Report via mail or email.
    Mayor Schlicht suggested that staff consider combining Mission Viejo Life and
  Outlook.
    Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that the smartphone app “Access Mission Viejo” is
  great.

13.  Capital Improvement Program

  The Council deferred discussion on the CIP projects and prioritization.

City Council Minutes  7  January 16, 2015
   Jim Montrella, member of the MV Nadadores Board of Directors, M.V.: stated that the
  Nadadores are 501c3 non-profit organization which, at one time, was sponsored by a
  private corporation. He noted that it is an honest, forthright organization and they have
  gotten along very well with prior City Councils. Mr. Montrella stated that he hopes that
  the present Council and staff will continue in a very forthright manner. Lastly, he
  addressed the question on public use of the facility by announcing that the Nadadores were
  ready to start public programs but knew the renovation was coming and didn't want to
  start them only to cancel or postpone them.

  When asked about three projects - Bocce Ball Courts, Felipe Tennis Lights Replacement,
  La Paz/Felipe Overlook, Council Member Sachs said continue them, but he questioned
  the lighting at Felipe. Mayor Schlicht does not want to continue forward with the La Paz
  Overlook. Council Member Bucknum, Council Member Ury and Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  said to continue with the projects, but La Paz Overlook is a lower priority.

  Other Council questions and observations:

    City has identified two bocce ball courts.
    Bocce shouldn’t interfere with the kids’ playing field.
    Should the City purchase Bocce Ball equipment or people bring their own?

  By consensus, all Council Members agreed that they would like to reinstate the previous
  policy of rehabilitating two playgrounds per year.

  By consensus, the Council Members felt it is too early for them to weigh in on whether
  Building/Facility Rehabilitation Projects should be in the budget or not. The Council
  wished to defer this topic for future discussion.

  Other Council questions and observations on Infrastructure and other projects:

    Council Member Sachs stated that the Aquatics Center fix does need to be done
  and asked if the City can match dollars for projects like the Aquatics Center. It’s
  an old-looking facility.
    Council Member Ury asked for an update on traffic signal coordination.
    Mayor Schlicht expressed concern about using park fees for the Aquatics Center
  rehab.
    The Council would like an update on where we are on traffic signal coordination.
    Suggestion to Mayor: create an ad hoc committee and have conversation with the
  Nadadores.
    The youth sports focus in Mission Viejo began with the Nadadores.
    The annual average cost for restroom maintenance is $11,000 per facility.

City Council Minutes  8  January 16, 2015
 RECESS

At the hour of 2:05 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 2:20
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

14.  Unfunded Liabilities

  By consensus, the Council all agreed that funding to 80% would be the goal of the first 2-
  year budget cycle and 85% in the next budget cycle

  Other comments and observations:

    Council Member Sachs noted the value to the citizens of Mission Viejo as
  shareholder’s:
  o 2011 ROI = $410.99 (based on population of 95,000)
  o 2012  = $366.38 (unfunded liabilities not on the books)
  o 2012  = $328.00 (after unfunded liabilities)
  o 2013  = $315.00
  How do we build this value? One significant way is to pay off unfunded liabilities,
  especially pension costs, sooner and that would reduce interest cost.
    How we manage the number of people the City employs is another way to manage
  future pension costs.

5.  Discretionary Reserves

  Council observations and questions:

    Don’t co-mingle types of reserves, e.g., facility rehabilitation and computer
  equipment. It costs money to make the website more transparent to the public and
  we have some dated IT equipment.
    Consider taking reserves to 40% to pay down debt and implement some desired
  projects for the community.
    Consider a managed equipment outsourcing service to save money and keep
  technology up to date. The staff would manage the service level for the contract.
  This service method can apply to all hard assets, e.g. vehicles. But immediate
  application that makes sense is with IT.
    Don’t create “use it or lose it” budgets.
    What is the policy/procedures to bring reserves below 50% to pay something off?
  No policy change if in the 40-50% range.
    Reserves policy is set by Council and can be changed by Council vote.

City Council Minutes  9  January 16, 2015
     Should re-examine useful life and replacement needs, e.g. when to replace
  vehicles.
    There may be more technology that could assist police.
    Third party agreements could be considered—possibly with other cities.

15.  Questions and Staff Direction

  The Council provided final prioritization of some of the topics discussed as follows:

  1.  Economic Development
  2.  Unfunded liabilities
  3.  Playgrounds
  4.  Decrease discretionary reserves
  5.  Marguerite Aquatics Center
  6.  Slope Maintenance

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 3:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 19, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 2, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  January 16, 2015
